title: Go SDK generics-based helpers for typed structs + streaming structured-output decoding
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Goal: Add ergonomic, type-safe helpers to the Go SDK so application teams can decode Redwood model responses directly into typed structs (including streaming partial results) with minimal boilerplate and clear fallbacks for unstructured output.

Background: Current Go SDK provides raw streaming of token deltas and an ad-hoc json.RawMessage path for structured output. That forces every team to write bespoke glue to convert JSON blobs into domain structs, and makes streaming structured decoding awkward. We want: (1) a simple Decode[T any](resp) helper for non-streaming responses, (2) a StreamingDecoder[T any] that can yield incremental typed updates as the model emits structured pieces, and (3) ergonomics for models that sometimes emit free text instead of JSON (robust fallback and partial decode).

Design proposal (high level):
- Add package redwood/streamdecode with two primary APIs: Decode[T any](ctx, req) (blocking) and StreamingDecoder[T any] (constructor takes io.Reader/chan of chunks).
- StreamingDecoder will be generics-based: type StreamingDecoder[T any] struct { r io.Reader; json *json.Decoder; buffer bytes.Buffer; } with methods: Next(ctx) (T, bool, error) where bool indicates whether this Next produced a meaningful typed update (false = more streaming data expected). Implement TryPartial() to return a best-effort partial T when a field is missing.
- Support two wire formats from Redwood responses: 1) Structured events that contain a "structured" field with complete JSON snippets; 2) Delta token stream for legacy models. The decoder will attempt to parse structured snippets first and fallback to assembling tokens and running a final schema unmarshal when the stream ends.
- Provide validation hooks: options functional pattern (WithValidator(func(T) error)) to allow schema checks and confidence scoring before returning a typed value. Also provide WithFallback(func(raw string) (T, error)) so consumers can plug prompt-correction heuristics (common for free-text fallbacks).

Ergonomics and trade-offs considered:
- Using generics keeps surface area small for consumers, but increases compile-time complexity for SDK maintainers. We will keep helper internals non-generic where possible and only expose a thin generic facade.
- Streaming typed decoding requires keeping state between chunks; we will keep the state in-memory per stream (cost: memory proportional to one request). For extremely long-running streams we provide a "max_buffer" option to force flush/error to avoid OOM.
- Error model: expose three categories via typed errors in text form: "ErrPartial" (valid partial object), "ErrInvalidSchema" (validation failed), "ErrStreamEOF" (no more data). Consumers can string-match or use provided helper IsPartial(err) for control flow.

API examples (pseudo-Go):
- Blocking helper:
  var out MySchema
  if err := streamdecode.Decode[MySchema](ctx, client.Call(req), &out); err != nil { return err }

- Streaming helper:
  dec := streamdecode.NewStreamingDecoder[MySchema](resp.Body, streamdecode.WithValidator(validateMySchema))
  for {
    obj, ok, err := dec.Next(ctx)
    if err != nil { log.Printf("stream error: %v", err); break }
    if ok { emit(obj) }
    if dec.Done() { break }
  }

Backward compatibility Strategy:
- Default behavior stays the same for existing callers. New helpers are opt-in.
- When a structured event arrives, decode immediately and continue. If receiver never emits a structured event, accumulate tokens and attempt final unmarshal at EOF. This supports models that occasionally switch forms.

Testing & QA:
- Unit tests for: complete structured event, interleaved structured + text tokens, pure text fallback, validator failures, max_buffer overflow.
- Add an integration test that runs against a local mock server that replays recorded Redwood streaming payloads (from /testdata/streams).
- Performance test to ensure streaming decoder doesn't regress single-request latency by >5% (microbenchmark is in pkg/streamdecode/bench).

Rollout plan:
1) Land internals and unit tests behind build tag 'streamdecode_exp' to allow early e2e without exposing to all users.
2) Merge public API with docs and examples (go-sdk v1.8-beta). Insert migration doc in docs/streaming-structured.md.
3) Beta test with two internal teams: Console (rollouts UI) and Optimize (evals ingestion). Collect feedback for 1 sprint.
4) Promote to GA and announce in release notes.

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/cp/Go-SDK-structured-decode (internal Confluence stub)
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/pull/1234 (WIP, comments requested)
- Integration test fixtures: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/sdk-go/stream-fixtures

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Should the SDK attempt to repair non-JSON model output (e.g., try to extract JSON block from free text) or should we expose that as an explicit opt-in fallback? (current leaning: opt-in WithFallback to avoid surprising behavior)
- Naming: StreamingDecoder vs. LiveDecoder. Prefer StreamingDecoder for clarity but open to bikeshedding.

Follow-ups (post-merge):
- Add TypeScript parity: a thin wrapper in typescript-sdk to keep feature parity (PM: please coordinate).
- Document migration patterns for customers who currently parse json.RawMessage from responses.
- Add telemetry: produce a metric for decode failures per-model to help identify problematic model variants.
